name: Medical Office Administration
description: The front office of a medical practice — scheduling, registration, insurance verification, referrals, correspondence, and the patient's first and last five minutes. ⚠⚠ The occupation it leads to is enormous: 850,000 medical secretaries and administrative assistants nationally, with 85,900 openings a year, more than four times the whole medical-records occupation. Taught at 36 Florida public institutions.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠ THE JOB MARKET IS LARGE AND THE CREDENTIAL MARKET IS NOT. Florida awards only 242 credentials a year across these codes — 80 under medical administrative assistant, 91 under medical office management, 57 under medical office assistant and 14 under facilities administration — into an occupation with 85,900 annual openings nationally. ⚠⚠⚠ The arithmetic says most people are hired into this work without the certificate, and O*NET's own figures agree: 48% enter with a high school diploma. ⚠ Read that honestly in both directions. You can get in without paying for a programme — and the programme is therefore something you should only buy if it gives you something the job will not, which usually means medical terminology, insurance verification and the electronic health record. ⚠⚠ THE CEILING IS THE PROBLEM, NOT THE ENTRY. This route has no credential ladder: there is no state licence, no national registry that employers filter on, and no accredited degree above it in the same subject. ⚠⚠⚠ So if you want somewhere to go afterwards, the move is sideways into HEALTH INFORMATION MANAGEMENT, where the associate degree makes you RHIT-eligible, or into BILLING AND CODING, where the CPC does. ⚠ Ask any programme what its graduates did next, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

cips.note: Medical Administrative/Executive Assistant and Medical Secretary — 32 Florida public institutions and 80 credentials, all one-to-two-year certificates. ⚠ The widest footprint of the three and the smallest output: many institutions run it, few people finish it, which is consistent with most people entering the occupation without it.
Medical Office Management/Administration — 8 Florida public institutions, 91 credentials. The supervisory end of the same work, and the closest thing this route has to a next rung.
Medical Office Assistant — 3 Florida public institutions, 57 credentials. A narrower, shorter version of the same subject; included so the schools that use this code are listed.

Hospital and Health Care Facilities Administration/Management — 6 Florida public institutions, 14 credentials. ⚠ Small, and included because it is where the administrative route touches the management one; the substantial version of that subject is health care administration at 51.0701.

related.note: ⚠⚠ The move worth knowing about, because this route has no ceiling of its own. HIM is taught at 31 Florida institutions and its ASSOCIATE DEGREE makes you eligible for the RHIT credential — which front-office experience plus a degree is a genuinely strong combination for, since you already know how a practice actually runs.

⚠ The other sideways move, and in a small practice you may already be doing half of it. 37 Florida institutions, and the CPC credential is something employers filter on where nothing filters on a medical secretary certificate. ⚠⚠ But read that programme's note on the CPC-A apprentice trap before treating it as a quick win.

⚠⚠ The closest comparison and often the better buy. Medical assisting covers the same administrative work — MEA0501 Medical Office Procedures, MEA0500 Medical Office Receptionist — AND adds the clinical half, and it has four labelled exit points where this has none. ⚠ If you are choosing between them and are not certain you want to stay out of clinical work, medical assisting keeps more doors open.
